findings_addressed.oracle: Mutation isolation on the real SandboxManager: after create() populates the real registry via _in_memory_sandbox_factory-patched WindowsSandbox, the returned list is cleared; a second call to instances must still yield length 1 because SandboxManager.instances returns list(self._instances.values()) -- a copy. An implementation that returns the live dict_values or a reference propagates the clear() and len(second_list) becomes 0.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/sandbox/manager.py line 148, change `return list(self._instances.values())` to `return self._instances.values()` -- clear() on the returned view object raises AttributeError OR a for-loop over the cleared view yields 0 items, so len(list(second_list)) == 0; the `len(second_list) == 1` assertion fails.

findings_addressed.oracle: UUID format contract on the real SandboxManager: str(uuid4()) always produces exactly 36 characters split into 5 segments by 4 hyphens at positions 8, 13, 18, 23 (lengths 8-4-4-4-12). Registry membership check `await mgr.get(inst.id) is inst` confirms the instance was stored under its own ID by the real manager.

findings_addressed.oracle: Real SandboxManager.get_status() is exercised end-to-end with _in_memory_sandbox_factory patched for WindowsSandbox/QEMUSandbox. Scalar oracles: max_instances == 5 (constructor arg), active_count == 1 (one auto_start=True instance), total_count == 1. Instance-entry oracle: key 'type' (not 'sandbox_type') == 'windows', 'id' == inst.id, 'status' == 'running'.
